summary: Verified bug fix for Re-optimizar Biblioteca admin tool. Backend pytest triggered /api/admin/reoptimize-library and polled status. Result: optimized=1, skipped=5, errors=0, saved_bytes=13,784,708 (~13.1 MB), done=6/6, percent=100. UI test logged in, opened Mirror DB tab, clicked Re-optimizar Biblioteca button — job completed without error. After the pytest already consumed the one giant master (shared object storage), the UI panel now correctly displays 'No hay masters grandes pendientes — la biblioteca ya está optimizada', confirming the persistent post-fix steady state. The bug 'optimized=0 for everything' is fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: Setting Pillow MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS=None globally is safe here because library masters are curated (Pexels/Unsplash) and processed one/two at a time as commented; just be aware this disables the decompression-bomb guard process-wide for any future untrusted upload paths.

optimize_image() still swallows generic Exception silently and returns the original bytes — fine for upload resilience but for the re-opt job consider logging.exception so any new failure mode (e.g. truncated source) doesn't quietly inflate 'skipped' count again.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Preview env already had 6 reopt candidates (1 giant 14MB JPEG + 5 already-optimized WebPs).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_reoptimize_library.py triggers a real reopt run. Object storage is shared, so after the first successful run the panel naturally shows zero pending masters and 'No hay masters grandes pendientes'. To see live progress numbers in the UI again, a new large unoptimized master needs to be seeded first.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: prior to fix, large JPEG (>178 MP) tripped Pillow's decompression-bomb DOS guard inside optimize_image(), exception caught -> original bytes returned -> _reopt_one saw size unchanged and counted as 'skipped'. Mitigation in /app/backend/server.py line 1310: _PILImage.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None lets giant trusted masters decode; resize to MAX_IMAGE_WIDTH=2000 and re-encode to WebP q80 shrinks them ~95%. Verified saved_bytes=13.78 MB on the single 14MB master in this run.
